gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Keychron K3 Max's four programmable layers are split two for Mac and two for Windows by the OS toggle, so a programmer gets one base layer and one Fn layer in whichever mode they use, not four.
standout_why: I opened seven of the result pages on 2026-11-21: mechkeyfoundry.com's best-of (cited) and three-way comparison, mkbguide.com, pcreviewer.org, zelobiz.com and pickedtech.com. All name the firmware (QMK/Launcher, NuPhyIO, VIA, Logi Options+), and several say 'create layers' or 'programmable layers'. None gives a layer count or mentions the Mac/Windows split. The two cited RTINGS pages (best low-profile, Air75 V3 review) returned only navigation to my fetch, so I could not check them; the standout score assumes they lack it. Battery (mAh, lights-off and lights-on hours), travel and the differing height measures are already on mkbguide and mechkeyfoundry, so normalising those would score 0-1.
decides: It qualifies ChatGPT's 'Keychron K3 Max, best for customization' label instead of overturning it: on stock firmware the K3 Max gives two layers per OS mode, and Keychron's manual warns that Windows-mode edits must go on Layer 2, not Layer 0. I could not source layer counts for the NuPhy Air75 V3 (NuPhyIO) or Lofree Flow 2 (VIA), so the table cannot yet rank the three on usable layers. Until those two cells are filled, the finding is a footnote on the K3 Max row, not a reason to move the Lofree Flow 2 84 (the board we link) up or down.

findings.label: Programmable layers, as the manual states them
findings.value: 4 layers in total: Layers 0 and 1 are Mac, Layers 2 and 3 are Windows
findings.source_title: Keychron K3 MAX Benutzerhandbuch (ManualsLib mirror of Keychron's user manual), page 7
findings.note: Manual text: 'Your keyboard includes four layers of key settings, providing versatile options for both Mac and Windows operating systems.' 'Mac Layers (Layer 0 and Layer 1)'. 'When the system toggle is switched to Mac, Layer 0 will be activated by default.' Layer 1 is reached with Fn + MO(1). This is a third-party mirror; Keychron's own manual page and PDF were not readable with my tools.

findings.label: Layers usable in one OS mode on stock firmware
findings.value: 2 (one base layer plus one Fn layer): Layers 2 and 3 in Windows mode, Layers 0 and 1 in Mac mode
findings.source_title: Keychron K3 MAX Benutzerhandbuch (ManualsLib mirror of Keychron's user manual), page 8
findings.note: Manual text: 'Windows Layers (Layer 2 and Layer 3)'. 'When the toggle is set to Windows, the system will activate Layer 2'. 'When using Windows mode, ensure that changes or customizations are applied to Layer 2, not Layer 0. This is a common oversight that can cause key mapping issues.' Arithmetic: 4 layers / 2 OS modes = 2 per mode. The manual does not name Linux; a Linux user is on whichever toggle position they choose.

findings.label: What 'programmable' means on each board, as the rival pages state it
findings.value: Keychron K3 Max: QMK, remapped in Keychron Launcher (browser) or VIA. NuPhy Air75 V3: NuPhyIO only, no QMK or VIA. Lofree Flow 2: VIA. Logitech MX Mechanical Mini: Logi Options+ on Windows and macOS, no QMK or VIA
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air75 V3 vs Lofree Flow 2 vs Keychron K3 Max (Mech Key Foundry)
findings.note: Rival-page statements, not maker pages. Quotes: 'Keychron's K3 Max runs QMK and remaps through Keychron Launcher or VIA'; the Air75 V3 'uses NuPhy's own NuPhyIO configurator rather than QMK or VIA'; 'The Lofree Flow 2 is VIA-compatible'. The Logitech line is from the same site's best-of page: https://mechkeyfoundry.com/best-low-profile-mechanical-keyboard-wireless/. This is the part of the angle the rivals already cover.

findings.label: Firmware change from the V2
findings.value: Moved from the V2's QMK/VIA to NuPhyIO 2.0
findings.source_title: Best Low-Profile Mechanical Keyboards (2026) | MKB Guide
findings.note: MKB Guide: 'The V3 moved from the V2's QMK/VIA stack to NuPhyIO 2.0, a genuine enthusiast trade-off'. This matters because ChatGPT's second answer still discusses the Air75 V2 as a QMK/VIA board while showing the V3 card. pickedtech.com labels it 'NuPhy IO (QMK-based)', which conflicts with mechkeyfoundry; I could not settle it on NuPhy's page.

findings.label: Maker-rated battery life: rival pages disagree
findings.value: 1,550 mAh; pcreviewer.org says 'up to 78 hours without backlight, according to the manufacturer'; mechkeyfoundry.com says Keychron publishes no hours figure
findings.source_title: Best Low-Profile Mechanical Keyboards for Typing in 2026 (pcreviewer.org)
findings.note: The conflicting statement is at https://mechkeyfoundry.com/best-low-profile-mechanical-keyboard-wireless/: 'Keychron does not publish a battery-life figure in hours for the K3 Max, only a 1,550 mAh cell.' Keychron's product page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so the conflict is unresolved; do not print an hours figure for the K3 Max from this.

findings.label: Maker-rated lights-off battery life, with implied average current (already on rival pages except the current)
findings.value: NuPhy Air75 V3: 4,000 mAh, up to 1,200 h lights off, 60-100 h lights on (about 3.3 mA implied lights off). Lofree Flow 2 84: 3,000 mAh, up to 120 h over Bluetooth backlight off, 17 h backlight on (about 25 mA implied)
findings.source_title: NuPhy Air75 V3 vs Lofree Flow 2 vs Keychron K3 Max (Mech Key Foundry)
findings.note: Arithmetic is mine: 4,000 mAh / 1,200 h = 3.3 mA; 3,000 mAh / 120 h = 25 mA. A 7.5x gap in implied draw suggests the two makers' 'lights off' conditions are not the same test; mkbguide.com words NuPhy's figure as 'under lab conditions'. Figures are relayed by the rival page, not read on the makers' pages. Dealectric's own record for the Flow 2 84 says about 14 h backlight on, against the 17 h these pages give.

findings.label: Height figures use different measures (already on a rival page)
findings.value: Lofree Flow 2 84: about 21.5 mm case depth. NuPhy Air75 V3: 13.2 mm 'chassis dimension'. Logitech MX Mechanical Mini: about 26.1 mm case depth. Keychron K3 Max: 17 mm front, 22 mm rear with keycaps
findings.source_title: Best Low-Profile Mechanical Keyboards (2026) | MKB Guide
findings.note: The K3 Max figures are from https://pcreviewer.org/low-profile-mechanical-keyboards-2026/ ('Keychron lists a front height of 17mm and a rear height of 22mm with keycaps'). The 13.2 mm NuPhy figure is a chassis measure, not total height with keycaps, so it does not compare with Lofree's 21.5 mm. None of these were read on the makers' pages.
